This script compares each outcome before and after the index visit in the RUSH-era cohort without a model: McNemar's test overall, and counts and percentages within each characteristic. It produces `mcnemar_results` and `crosstabs`, the raw numbers behind the proportions the article reports.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/03_paired_comparisons.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/03_paired_comparisons.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

## McNemar's test

For engagement and retention, McNemar's test on each patient's pair of values ([Methodological background](methodological_background.qmd#mcnemars-test)), with the proportions before and after. It uses the wide data, one row per patient, because a pair is one row there. The original code ran it to confirm that the conditional logistic regression in the next script gives the same answer; for matched pairs the model's score test is McNemar's chi-squared test, while the model's reported Wald P value tests the same hypothesis and is close but not identical. If no pair is discordant there is nothing to test: the statistics are missing and `n_discordant` is 0, and the script carries on.

**Decision pending:** the original code did not run McNemar's test for viral suppression, though the article's Methods describe it for all three outcomes. Whether to add it is decision issue [#3](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-RUSH/issues/3).

## Crosstabs by characteristic

For every outcome and every characteristic, the counts and row percentages after the visit and before it, keeping missing values: the original code's nested loop of `tab … if Intervention==1, row missing`. These are the percentages within subgroups that the article quotes, such as engagement among patients aged 16 to 24 ([Published results](published_results.qmd#engagement-in-care)). The result is a nested list, `crosstabs[[outcome]][[characteristic]]$after`, so any one table can be pulled out by name.
